forces.title: Rising low-priced imports and elevated raw material costs compress paper realisations
forces.description: India’s Writing & Printing Paper industry faces severe pressure on realisations due to a sharp increase in low-priced imports, particularly from China and ASEAN, which grew over 80% from FY21 to FY26. Concurrently, production costs are inflated by high prices of key inputs like hardwood pulp, domestic wood, and wastepaper. This combination of intense import competition and elevated raw material costs significantly squeezes operating margins for Indian paper manufacturers.

forces.title: Domestic spinning capacity reduction improves industry pricing power
forces.description: Around 10-12 million spindles, approximately 20% of India's installed cotton yarn spinning capacity, have exited the market over the past few years. This reduction, concentrated among smaller, less efficient units, has led to significant industry consolidation. The resulting tighter demand-supply balance has improved the pricing power of the remaining organised and efficient players, creating a more sustainable pricing environment and enhancing profitability prospects for the sector.

forces.title: Strong demand recovery and export momentum for cotton yarn
forces.description: Demand for Indian cotton yarn has significantly strengthened across both domestic and export markets. Key drivers include easing US tariff uncertainties, improved order flows, and positive anticipation around Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) with the India-UK and India-EU blocs. China has emerged as a primary growth driver for exports, with a 121% surge in FY26. This robust demand is expected to support revenue growth and margin expansion for the cotton yarn industry.

forces.title: Restored parity between domestic and international cotton prices boosts competitiveness
forces.description: A critical factor behind the recovery of cotton yarn spreads is the restoration of parity between Indian and global cotton prices. In previous periods (FY23 and beyond), Indian cotton traded at a premium, eroding export competitiveness. With domestic prices now broadly aligned with international benchmarks, Indian manufacturers have regained a significant competitive edge in global markets. This alignment directly contributes to improved profitability and export performance.

forces.title: Growing global apparel market driven by lifestyle trends and e-commerce
forces.description: The global apparel market, valued at US$ 1.9 trillion in 2025, is projected to grow at a 4.1% CAGR from 2026 to 2034. This growth is significantly driven by rising demand for casualwear and athleisure, influenced by social media trends, increasing disposable incomes, and the continuous expansion of e-commerce platforms. These factors create substantial opportunities for Indian textile and apparel manufacturers and exporters to capture a larger share of the expanding global market.
forces.source_title: Textiles And Apparel Industry In India

forces.title: Favorable policy support and trade agreements boost textile exports
forces.description: Several government initiatives and trade agreements are providing a strong tailwind for India's textile exports. These include 100% FDI under the automatic route, significant budget allocations (US$ 597.34 million in Union Budget FY26-27), and focused projects like the Cotton Mission. Crucially, the India-UK Free Trade Agreement offers transformative opportunities, enhancing competitiveness for textiles, leather, and footwear in the UK market by potentially eliminating tariffs and expanding global reach for Indian goods.
forces.source_title: Textiles And Apparel Industry In India

forces.title: PM MITRA Parks strengthen integrated textile manufacturing infrastructure
forces.description: The 'Mega Integrated Textile Region and Apparel (MITRA) Park’ scheme, with a total outlay of US$ 502.97 million for implementation up to FY28, aims to establish seven state-of-the-art textile parks. These parks provide integrated manufacturing infrastructure, common utilities, and R&D labs, attracting significant investments (e.g., Warangal park attracting over US$ 679 million) and generating substantial employment. This initiative is designed to boost large-scale textile manufacturing and enhance global competitiveness by creating robust, efficient value chains.
forces.source_title: Textiles And Apparel Industry In India

forces.title: Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme boosts textile manufacturing
forces.description: A PLI scheme with an outlay of US$ 1.44 billion is expected to significantly boost textile manufacturers. The scheme incentivizes Man-Made Fibre (MMF) apparel, MMF fabrics, and 10 segments of technical textile products. These incentives, available for five years from FY26-30, aim to promote incremental turnover, reduce import dependence, strengthen domestic manufacturing, and integrate Indian companies more deeply into global supply chains. This policy support enhances profitability and competitiveness.
forces.source_title: Textiles And Apparel Industry In India

forces.title: Technical textiles emerge as a new arena of growth and export opportunity
forces.description: Technical textiles are revolutionizing the Indian textile industry, offering innovative solutions across diverse sectors such as automotive, healthcare, and construction. The market is projected for substantial growth, from US$ 29 billion in 2024 to US$ 309 billion by 2047. Policy support like the National Technical Textile Mission (NTTM) and the India-UK CETA, which grants 100% duty-free access, are expected to significantly boost exports (e.g., to US$ 1 billion by 2030 in the UK) and foster R&D.
forces.source_title: Textiles And Apparel Industry In India

forces.title: Rising micro and small enterprises (MSEs) drive development in textiles and G&J
forces.description: The growth and development in both the gems & jewellery and textiles sectors are significantly driven by Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs). These smaller players contribute to job creation, foster innovation, and diversify market offerings. Their rising participation indicates an increasingly dynamic and decentralized industry structure, supporting overall growth, particularly in labor-intensive segments. This trend suggests a robust entrepreneurial ecosystem and increased competitive intensity.
forces.source_title: Gems And Jewellery Industry In India

forces.title: Increasing FDI inflows create favorable conditions for textile and diamond processing
forces.description: India allows 100% FDI under the automatic route in the textiles sector and also in the gems & jewellery sector, including gold and diamond processing and trading. This policy fosters favorable conditions for foreign investors to expand their presence, leading to increased capital inflows. For textile manufacturing and diamond processing, these investments bring advanced technology, best practices, and enhanced global market access, contributing to capacity building and competitiveness.
forces.source_title: Gems And Jewellery Industry In India

forces.title: Mandatory hallmarking regime enhances trust and formalization in jewellery
forces.description: The mandatory BIS hallmarking scheme for gold jewellery, including details like BIS logo, purity, and HUID number, ensures authenticity, traceability, and quality assurance for consumers. While primarily for gold, such stringent quality norms promote formalization across the broader jewellery sector, including diamond ornaments. This structural change builds consumer confidence, attracts organized players, and reduces the informal market, fostering long-term growth and transparency for diamond processing and jewellery manufacturing.
forces.source_title: Gems And Jewellery Industry In India

forces.title: Expansion into lab-grown diamond jewellery segment
forces.description: Companies like Titan and Limelight Diamonds are aggressively entering and expanding in the lab-grown diamond jewellery segment. Titan launched its 'beYon' brand for affordable, everyday-wear lab-grown diamond jewellery, while Limelight Diamonds targets over 200 stores by 2027. This signifies a growing market for ethical and affordable alternatives to natural diamonds, driving innovation and new business opportunities for diamond cutting/polishing firms within IN040202.
forces.source_title: Gems And Jewellery Industry In India

forces.title: Government initiatives and R&D funding boost technical textile innovation
forces.description: The National Technical Textiles Mission (NTTM) is a significant tailwind, with 168 R&D projects approved for speciality fibres and applications (US$ 58.84 million outlay) and a US$ 127.72 million corpus dedicated to R&D. The 'Grant for Research & Entrepreneurship across Aspiring Innovators in Technical Textiles (GREAT)' scheme supports start-ups, and academic institutes are receiving grants to introduce technical textile courses. This strong policy and funding support fosters innovation, skill development, and competitive advantage in the technical textiles segment.
forces.source_title: Textiles And Apparel Industry In India

forces.title: Promotion of Khadi strengthens traditional textile sector and indigenous products
forces.description: The Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) continues to strengthen the Khadi sector through market linkages, brand promotion, and e-commerce integration. KVIC reported record provisional sales of US$ 21.17 billion in FY26, with Khadi textile sales reaching US$ 0.89 billion. Support schemes like MMDA, ISEC, and marketing assistance for sales outlets reflect growing consumer demand and increased promotion of indigenous products. This is a significant tailwind for traditional textile manufacturers.
forces.source_title: Textiles And Apparel Industry In India

forces.title: Moderation in textile manufacturing activity noted in May 2026
forces.description: The Manufacturing of Textiles Index stood at 104.1 in May 2026, registering a decline of 2.7% compared to May 2025. This indicates a moderation in overall textile manufacturing activity. While specific reasons are not detailed, such a decline suggests potential short-term headwinds related to demand fluctuations, input costs, or other operational challenges. This trend requires close monitoring as it impacts production volumes and capacity utilization across the sector.
forces.source_title: Textiles And Apparel Industry In India

viewpoints.title: Cotton yarn industry poised for improved profitability and revenue growth in FY27
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings projects a positive outlook for the Indian cotton yarn industry in FY27. This recovery is supported by structural supply correction, improved demand across domestic and export markets, easing US tariff uncertainties, and growing optimism from India-UK and India-EU Free Trade Agreements. The alignment of domestic and international cotton prices has restored export competitiveness. Operating margins are expected to expand by 150-200 bps in FY27, with revenue growth around 10%.

viewpoints.title: Indian cotton yarn industry's growth hinges on global competitiveness and policy support
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings acknowledges the healthier operating environment for the cotton yarn industry due to supply correction and improved demand. However, the sustainability of this improvement depends on several external factors, including Chinese demand trends, cotton price movements, geopolitical developments, and the pace of benefits from trade agreements. Long-term resilience also requires clearer policy support, cost optimisation, and backward integration to maintain global competitiveness and navigate demand volatility.

viewpoints.title: India's technical textile industry to exceed US$10 billion target by 2030
viewpoints.description: The Union Minister of Textiles expressed strong confidence in the future of India’s technical textile industry. He anticipates the sector will not only meet but surpass the ambitious target of US$10 billion in exports by 2030. This optimistic outlook underscores the government's belief in the sector's potential for innovation, advanced manufacturing capabilities, and its growing importance in global trade, positioning India as a key player in specialized fabrics.
viewpoints.source_firm: Union Minister of Textiles, Mr. Giriraj Singh (via IBEF)
viewpoints.source_title: Textiles And Apparel Industry In India

viewpoints.title: Indian technical textiles market has strong potential with significant growth rate
viewpoints.description: Ms. Rachna Shah, Secretary of the Ministry of Textiles, highlighted the significant potential of India's technical textiles market, noting its robust growth rate of 10%. She emphasized its position as the 5th largest globally, underscoring its strategic importance. This viewpoint reinforces the sector's trajectory towards becoming a major contributor to the Indian economy, driven by innovation and specialized applications across various industries like automotive and healthcare.
viewpoints.source_firm: Secretary of the Ministry of Textiles, Ms. Rachna Shah (via IBEF)
viewpoints.source_title: Textiles And Apparel Industry In India

viewpoints.title: Cotton yarn sector poised for substantial revenue growth in FY26
viewpoints.description: Crisil Ratings forecasts a 7-9% increase in revenue for India's cotton yarn sector in FY26, indicating a strong positive outlook. This projection is underpinned by factors such as rising demand and improved operating conditions, reflecting a robust recovery and expansion phase for yarn manufacturers. The anticipated growth highlights the sector's resilience and its capacity to capitalize on favorable market dynamics, strengthening its position within the broader textile industry.
viewpoints.source_title: Textiles And Apparel Industry In India
